podcasts.name: No Priors
podcasts.title: Powering AI-Driven Drug Discovery with President of Isomorphic Labs Max Jaderberg
podcasts.description: Drug discovery and development has long relied on expensive, time-consuming empirical trial and error. By shifting the discovery process onto computers, Isomorphic Labs wants to fundamentally change medicine from a process of discovery to one of precision engineering. Elad Gil sits down with Isomorphic’s president Max Jaderberg to discuss his vision for using predictive AI models to achieve experimental accuracy. Max details how the success of AlphaFold provided the first proof of concept that a deep learning model could generalize in the field of biology, and how an AI model’s compounding of learnings allows it to achieve generalizability with scale, thus greatly increasing the probability of success as well as speed in real world clinical trials. He also talks about evolving past the need for animal testing through in-silico models, Isomorphic’s focus on developing drug design engines that are agnostic of disease area, target class, and modality, why accurate molecule engineering unlocks the potential for multidrug cocktails that span complex biological pathways, and how he believes AI molecule optimization will improve both human lifespan and healthspan. podcasts.description: Thesis: 2027 is made possible by our founding partners, Lovable and Notion. Lovable is the fastest way to turn ideas into software people love: https://link.lovable.dev/every Notion is the collaborative AI workspace where teams and agents work side by side: https://www.notion.com/?utm_source=youtube&utm_campaign=thesis-2027&utm_content=every-261111-video What does great human work look like after automation? It’s a question we try to answer every day at Every, and the one we built our conference, Thesis, around. In his closing keynote, Dan Shipper argues that as AI makes intelligence cheap and widely available, what matters most is human perspective. It’s your “non-consensus” point of view, plus your responsibility for a particular corner of the world, that helps you spot the insight no one else would. On this week’s episode of The Every Podcast, we’re sharing Dan’s full talk at Thesis: 2027. Dan explains why benchmark charts make the future of work look bleaker than it is, why picking the right idea still takes a human, and how we should really measure AI models. podcasts.name: The Cognitive Revolution
podcasts.title: The Neuron Basis: Goodfire's Curt Tigges on Agentic Interp, Monosemanticity & Reverse Engineering
podcasts.description: Goodfire technical staff member Curt Tigges discusses research revealing that individual MLP neurons in modern language models are far more interpretable and functionally bounded than previously thought. Using an automated agent to test hypotheses across architectures like Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, Tigges explains how modern gated MLPs act as legible conjunctions and control signals capable of extensive dynamic sparsity without lasting benchmark loss. By showing that many internal representations can be directly enumerated, this work offers an alternative to complex external featurizers and provides practical avenues for behavior monitoring and persona steering.
